name: Audit the Meta ad account end to end
what: Read the whole Meta ad account (structure, naming, creative, tracking, spend) and produce one ranked 90 day roadmap naming the single biggest constraint, not a list of screenshots.
encompasses: Pull account, campaign, ad set and ad level data for the trailing 12 months from the gallery cache and a fresh Meta re-pull
Run the structure review checklist: campaign purpose lines, ad set count vs spend tier, naming, CBO vs ABO use
Run the creative review in fixed order: volume, then diversity, then quality
Score the account on a readable-data test (can results be read without guessing) and a commercial-alignment test (does spend match the business's real priorities)
Validate any proposed structure against 4 fixed questions before it goes in the roadmap
Rank findings by money at stake, not by how easy they are to fix
Write the roadmap as dated, ranked actions with the metric each one should move
inputs: connector: meta ads read (gallery cache + MCP re-pull)
founder_sees: One ranked list: here is the one thing most limiting Meta results right now, and what it would take to fix it.

name: Audit the Google Ads account end to end
what: Read the whole Google Ads account and diagnose problems top down: business, channel, campaign, metric, then root cause, following the 3 pre diagnosis rules before changing anything.
encompasses: Pull account and campaign structure, spend and conversions (manual export until a connector exists)
Diagnose any dip top down: business level, then channel share, then campaign, then metric, then root cause
Apply the 3 pre diagnosis rules before touching any setting
Find the inflection date of a change and check only the top 5 campaigns by spend around it
Match the failure mode checklist to the campaign type that dipped (Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen)
Split CPA and clicks into their formula parts (impressions, CTR, CVR) to find the real cause
Default to an isolated fix over a full rebuild unless the isolated fix has already failed
inputs: connector: google ads (manual export, no read connector yet)
tools: web: Google Ads UI export (no connector yet)
founder_sees: A plain diagnosis of why Google spend is underperforming, in the order the problem actually happened, and one fix to try first.

name: Check Meta pixel, CAPI and customer sync health
what: Confirm every order and its value passes cleanly from checkout to the Meta pixel and CAPI, and that new, engaged and existing customer segments are defined and syncing.
encompasses: Check that purchase events fire with the real order value, not a fixed or missing value
Check event match quality and event deduplication between pixel and CAPI
Define new, engaged and existing customer audience segments from the brand's own data
Check the customer list sync runs on schedule and matches current order data
Flag any gap between store order count and Meta reported purchases
inputs: connector: meta ads read (ads_pixel_event_read, ads_get_datasets, ads_get_dataset_quality)
outputs: developer brief for any pixel or CAPI fix
registry entry if a fix is approved
tools: mcp: meta ads read (ads_get_dataset_quality, ads_get_dataset_stats, ads_pixel_event_read, ads_pixel_parameter_read)
founder_sees: Whether Meta can actually see and value the brand's real orders, and what is broken if not.

name: Build and audit Google conversion tracking
what: Set one primary purchase action, pass real order value through enhanced conversions, and pick the tracking route (app, GTM, server side) by the brand's spend level, then check it against Shopify monthly.
encompasses: Set exactly one primary purchase conversion action, optimised to purchase, never add to cart or clicks
Never use the GA4 import as the primary purchase action
Turn on enhanced conversions and pass real order value
Pick the tracking build route by spend: app first, then GTM, then server side above about $50k a month
Add the Conversion Linker tag on all pages and turn on auto tagging
Pass product ID, category and value in dynamic remarketing tag parameters
Set conversion windows to match the purchase cycle, then check against Shopify
Track new customers with their own event, not Google's acquisition setting
Use add to cart as the primary goal only for high ticket, low volume products
Reconcile Google reported purchases against backend orders after setup and every month
inputs: brand brain: order feed, product catalogue
connector: google ads and GTM (no read connector yet, manual)
trigger: event: new account or quarterly recheck
tools: web: Google Tag Manager and Google Ads UI (no connector yet)
founder_sees: Whether Google can be trusted to report real orders and real order values, with a brief a developer can implement.

name: Reconcile platform ROAS against blended MER
what: Compare each platform's own reported ROAS against acquisition MER (total new customer revenue over total spend) before any keep, kill or scale call, and treat incremental lift as a check column, never the optimisation target.
encompasses: Compute platform ROAS and acquisition MER from the metric contract, in code
Use the same attribution setting on every campaign inside one platform
Never tighten Google attribution windows to match Meta, or copy Meta rules onto Google
Reconcile TikTok reported purchases with store orders on 7 day click
Reconcile marketplace sales and payment-method returns (chargebacks and disputes; cash-on-delivery returns, India only) separately before trusting platform ROAS
Run a monthly platform ROAS versus aMER reconciliation using the attribution comparison columns
Judge an assist layer (view through, upper funnel) by downstream lag, not its own last click ROAS
Sanity check any too good ROAS number against attribution window and audience segment before acting on it
Treat daily ROAS swings under about $1,000 a day as normal noise, not a signal
inputs: connector: meta ads read, gallery sales.json (Metabase)
connector: google ads and TikTok (manual, no connector yet)
outputs: flag list of platforms disagreeing with store data
founder_sees: Whether the ad platforms' own numbers can be trusted, and what the real blended return is once store data is the judge.

name: Run incrementality and lift tests
what: Design and read a Conversion Lift or geo lift test when platform ROAS and blended MER still disagree after attribution is tightened, to find the ad spend that would not have converted anyway.
encompasses: Confirm attribution has already been tightened and reconciled before proposing a lift test
Choose test type: Meta Conversion Lift, geo holdout, or matched-market geo test
Size the test: markets or audience split, minimum spend, and read window
Write the test brief: hypothesis, holdout design, read point, and what counts as proof
Read the result and update the brand's effect prior for that spend level
Never let a lift test change platform bidding directly; feed the result into budget decisions instead
trigger: event: attribution disagreement persists after reconciliation
tools: mcp: meta ads read (ads_experiment_lift_get_test, ads_experiment_list_tests, ads_experiment_check_eligibility)
founder_sees: A clear test that answers whether this spend is buying orders that would not have happened anyway, with a plain yes or no plan to run it.

name: Filter platform automated suggestions before applying them
what: Log and test every Ads Manager or Google Ads suggestion before it is applied, and separate real targeting controls from settings that are only suggestions.
encompasses: Log every platform suggested change with its stated expected effect
Test each suggestion in a small sandbox before wider rollout, where testable
Audit which targeting fields are real controls and which are non-binding suggestions
Turn off auto apply recommendations and AI generated assets by default
Record the actual effect of any suggestion that was applied, against the platform's claim
inputs: connector: meta ads read, google ads (manual)
outputs: change list (apply or reject, with reason)
founder_sees: A short list of what the platform wants to change automatically, whether it was tested, and whether it actually helped last time.

name: Score new customer economics and set ROAS or CAC targets from margin
what: Build a monthly new customer view (CAC, first purchase gross profit, GP to CAC) and set every ROAS or CPA target from the brand's own contribution margin, never an industry benchmark.
encompasses: Compute break even ROAS and break even CPA from contribution margin, in code
Confirm unit economics before setting any scale plan
Build the monthly new customer P&L: CAC, first purchase gross profit, GP to CAC
Score GP to CAC against fixed bands to decide hold, scale, or spend more
Set each product category's ROAS target from its own gross margin, not one account wide number
Raise AOV before cutting acquisition cost when AOV is low for the category
Build GP cohort growth curves at day 90, 180 and 365 to set the real CAC tolerance
inputs: brand brain: cogs, margin by SKU
metric contract: cpa, gross_margin, ltv_180d, contribution_margin
founder_sees: What it actually costs to win a new customer by category, and the ROAS or CPA target that matches the brand's own margin, not a generic rule of thumb.

name: Design Meta account structure by spend tier
what: Pick and build the campaign structure template that matches the brand's monthly Meta spend: small, mid or large, and keep the account inside its readable data and commercial alignment tests.
encompasses: Use the small spend template: one testing campaign, optional scaling, optional small retention campaign
Use the mid spend template: 2 to 3 cold campaigns with a stated reason and higher ad volume
Use the large spend template: mandatory page strategy and bidding diversity across campaigns
Merge campaigns whose conversion volume is too thin to optimise well
Fully consolidate to one campaign only for a single product, single persona, small spend store
Split campaigns by business unit, ad sets by concept, never by launch date
Plan extra ad pages before hitting the live ad per page cap
outputs: change list for campaign consolidation or split
trigger: event: spend tier change or after audit
founder_sees: The account structure that matches current spend, as a diagram and a list of changes for someone to make.

name: Write campaign purpose lines and naming convention
what: Require a one line defendable purpose for every campaign and a fixed naming pattern for every ad set, so reporting problems get fixed with naming, not new campaigns.
encompasses: Write a one line purpose for every existing and new campaign
Fix reporting or readability problems with naming and filters before adding new campaigns
Run recurring promos in their own campaign, named for the promo
Name every ad set with persona, angle, offer, content type and launch date, never a batch name
Name ad set forks with the same concept fields plus launch date so results can be tracked across forks
founder_sees: One naming rule for the whole account, and which campaigns or ad sets do not follow it yet.

name: Design ad set and concept architecture
what: Define a concept as one SKU, one pain point and one offer, keep non overlapping personas apart, and load each concept ad set with enough ads for 2 to 6 exposures before purchase.
encompasses: Define a concept as SKU, pain point and offer; a change to any one starts a new ad set
Load each concept ad set with enough ads for 2 to 6 exposures before purchase, minimum 3
Launch every new concept with the concept ad plus 3 hook variations
Keep non overlapping personas out of the same ad set
Group all funnel stages for one persona in one ad set, or blend the numbers before deciding to split by stage
Spin a funnel into its own campaign once it is big enough to KPI alone
Run recurring promos in their own campaign, isolated from evergreen concepts
founder_sees: How a new idea becomes one ad set, with which personas and offers can share it and which cannot.

name: Build Meta audiences: broad, custom, lookalike, exclusions
what: Go broad in cold targeting by default, cap any interest or lookalike test as a small sandbox, and exclude existing customers from every cold campaign sized to the repurchase cycle.
encompasses: Go broad in cold targeting and let the page, price and reviews qualify the buyer
Cap any interest, lookalike or custom audience test as a small sandbox
Put the target audience in the creative and copy, not in the targeting settings
Exclude existing customers from every cold campaign, sized to the brand's repurchase cycle
Define and refresh new, engaged and existing customer segments on schedule
inputs: brand brain: customer list, repurchase cycle
trigger: event: new campaign or quarterly refresh
founder_sees: Which audiences to build or refresh, and which existing customers to keep out of cold campaigns.

name: Set placements and turn off automatic creative edits
what: Remove weak placements from store campaigns, and turn off Advantage+ creative edits and flexible or dynamic crop on every product ad so the brand's own image and copy show as made.
encompasses: Never launch placement, age or gender campaigns from breakdown ROAS alone
Remove Audience Network app rewards placement from store or engaged view campaigns
Turn off flexible or dynamic crop ads on catalogue and product ads
Turn off Advantage+ creative edits on every product ad
outputs: change list (placement exclusions, creative edit toggles)
trigger: event: after audit or new campaign
founder_sees: Which placements to drop and which auto edit settings to turn off so ads look the way the brand made them.

name: Choose Meta bid strategy and cost caps
what: Default to CBO for efficiency, switch to ABO at high AOV with low daily order volume, and win impressions with a sharper hook and clearer offer instead of raising the bid.
encompasses: Default to CBO for efficiency; switch to ABO at high AOV with low daily order volume
At large spend, run CBO with ad set minimum and maximum spend limits instead of pure CBO
Test a seasonal rotation: CBO in Q4 peak, ABO in Q1 for clean testing
Ignore cost and bid caps under about $200k a month; pick a bid strategy by business constraint
Set cost caps and bidding at ad set level, never at ad level
Win impressions with a sharper hook and clearer offer instead of raising the bid
Test whether a higher on page action rate lowers CPM before assuming a bid change is needed
trigger: event: after audit or spend tier change
founder_sees: Which bid setting fits the account's spend and AOV right now, and why raising the bid is not the first lever to pull.

name: Size Meta creative tests and read windows
what: Size every creative test with a kill rule threshold of 3x to 5x target CPA, use the budget formula (target conversions times CPA divided by test days) instead of Meta's learning phase rule, and check the test budget can actually reach that spend in the test window.
encompasses: Size every creative test with a kill rule threshold: 3x to 5x target CPA before judging
Size test budgets with the formula: target conversions times CPA divided by test days
Never derive test budgets from Meta's 50 conversions in 7 days learning rule
Match test read windows to purchase cycle and volume; never read under 5 days below $50k a month
Never judge or kill an ad on $1 to $2 of spend
Check that every ad set's planned budget can actually reach its read spend threshold in the test window
outputs: test brief with budget and read window
founder_sees: How much to spend and how long to wait before judging a new ad, and the exact number where it gets killed or kept.

name: Set creative volume, diversity and refresh targets
what: Launch about 1 new ad per $1,000 of monthly spend, hit the concept count band for the spend tier, test ads that differ by benefit, price or persona rather than crop or color, and plan a yearly refresh to offset CPM inflation.
encompasses: Launch about 1 new ad per $1,000 of monthly spend, with diminishing returns at very large spend
Hit the concept count band for the account's spend tier
Test ads that differ by benefit, price point or persona, not just crop or color
Plan a yearly creative and page refresh to offset CPM inflation
Inside a winning ad set, use spend share only to brief new creative, never to move budget
Track ad format as a spend share signal inside concept ad sets, not as a separate ad set split
Run the creative review in a fixed order: volume, then diversity, then quality
Diversify creative before a narrow persona callout saturates its cluster and drifts to colder audiences
Favor static ads over video when creative capacity is limited
Audit the creative library by awareness stage against an 80/10/10 split
Audit unintended buyer signals a creative sends before launch
Audit which Meta targeting fields the creative itself is quietly narrowing
founder_sees: How many new ads are needed this month, what mix of angles and formats is missing, and where the creative pipeline is thin.

name: Apply kill, keep and scale rules to ad sets
what: Judge and move budget at the ad set level on a keep, yellow, kill table read at 3x to 5x target CPA, never touch a winning ad set directly, and find each winner's spend equilibrium by stepping budget until ROAS turns unprofitable.
encompasses: Judge and move budget at the ad set level, never on a single ad's ROAS
Apply the keep, yellow, kill decision table at 3x to 5x target CPA
Never touch a winning ad set; fork new creative into a new ad set beside it
Never run creative tests inside the scaling campaign
Do not ride one winner; clone it into variants and keep a creative pipeline running
Rescue high conviction, CBO starved ads in a small separate ad set, capped and logged
Raise winning ad set budgets in steps sized to the read window, not a fixed percentage
Find each winner's spend equilibrium by stepping budget up until ROAS turns unprofitable, then pull back
Move only confirmed equilibrium winners into a dedicated scaling campaign
Judge every budget raise over 7 or more days, never on same day revenue
Confirm a winner acquires new customers under 7 day click before briefing more of it
When doubling down on a winner, shift creative volume toward it and build the funnel around it
Flag high frequency on a top spending prospecting ad before scaling it further
founder_sees: A daily list: which ad sets to kill, which to leave alone, which to scale, and by how much.

name: Read frequency and diagnose creative fatigue
what: Read 30 day frequency by audience segment rather than a blended number, and when frequency rises with flat cold reach, fix the creative mix by awareness stage before touching exclusions.
encompasses: Read 30 day frequency by audience segment, not as a blended percentage
When frequency rises with flat cold reach, fix the creative mix by awareness stage before touching exclusions
Watch frequency and ROAS trend together on narrow persona ads and brief a new concept when ROAS taper starts
Watch per ad video retention curves and fix drops at the product intro or call to action
outputs: creative brief request to MCR/ADC specialist
tools: gallery: insights tab (video metrics, creative lifecycle)
founder_sees: Which ads and segments are wearing out, and whether the fix is new creative or a targeting change.

name: Run existing customer and retargeting campaigns
what: Hold all existing customer spend in one dedicated campaign sized in dollars and frequency, ask cold spend to grow and retargeting spend to shrink where possible, and retarget non buyers with a different offer or objection, not the same ad louder.
encompasses: Ask 'where can cold spend grow' for prospecting and 'where can this shrink' for retargeting
Skip a website visitor retargeting campaign unless the engaged segment is starved of cold spend
Size existing customer ad budget in dollars and frequency, never as a percentage of spend
Hold all existing customer spend in one dedicated campaign so it cannot bleed into cold
Do not hyper segment retargeting by funnel stage, warmth tier or page viewed
Retarget non buyers with a different offer, proof or objection handling ad, not the same ad louder
Time win back or reminder ads to land just before a customer's typical reorder date
For high AOV considered purchases, run a longer nurture ladder before a same day retargeting push
Run a dedicated lapsed customer campaign with its own strategy
inputs: brand brain: repurchase cycle, customer segments
trigger: event: after audit or quarterly review
founder_sees: How much of the budget is warm traffic, whether that is too much or too little, and what to say to non buyers instead of repeating the same ad.

name: Manage dynamic product ads and the catalogue feed
what: Keep DPA out of the cold CBO in its own capped ad set, and read its results on 7 day click or incremental attribution, never on its blended platform ROAS.
encompasses: Keep DPA out of the cold CBO in its own ad set, and cap its share of total spend
Read DPA on 7 day click or incremental attribution, never on its blended platform ROAS
Check the product catalogue feed for missing images, prices or availability before scaling DPA
Check the customer and product sync into the catalogue is current
tools: mcp: meta ads read (ads_catalog_get_diagnostics, ads_catalog_get_dynamic_ads_health, ads_catalog_list_products)
founder_sees: Whether the catalogue feed is healthy enough to trust DPA, and how DPA is really performing once read correctly.

name: Plan the peak sale ramp and wind down
what: Ramp budget and structure ahead of a peak sale, fix a wind down date before the sale starts, and prepare the Google account for a known sale date ahead of time rather than after it opens.
encompasses: Set the ramp schedule: budget steps, new creative, and structure changes before the sale window
Fix a wind down date and budget step down before the sale starts, not during it
Prepare Google Shopping, Search and brand campaigns for the known sale date in advance
Check stock levels against the planned ramp before committing budget
Write the post sale review checklist and read point
inputs: brand brain: sale calendar, stock levels
trigger: event: 3 to 4 weeks before a known sale
founder_sees: The budget and structure plan for the next sale, with a fixed date to wind it back down.

name: Set up cross border and multi market ad delivery

encompasses: Give cross border buyers their own currency, delivery time and duty messaging in ad copy
Set local payment methods, language and currency defaults for a mobile first, non US market
Show shipping cost and import duty in the Google feed for cross border orders
Run one Google feed per currency

founder_sees: What needs to change in ads and feeds before selling to a new country or a cross border buyer.

name: Manage ad account access, ownership and multi account scaling
what: Keep the ad account, Merchant Center and analytics under one master login, lock down Business Center access before adding a team, and only open a second ad account on the same pixel once spend passes about $250k a month.
encompasses: Put the ad account, Merchant Center and analytics under one master login
Lock down TikTok and Meta Business access before adding any team member
Open a second ad account on the same pixel only once spend passes about $250k a month
Do not split ad accounts by country except to bill in local currency
Audit who has admin, employee or partner access on every connected account

external_write.surface: meta ads / tiktok ads / google ads

Test every TikTok pixel event before launch and stop if purchase or add to cart does not fire

Read the first test at 24 hours on soft metrics and at 3 days on cost metrics, then cut the bottom half

Seed TikTok lookalikes from purchasers or visitors instead of targeting them directly
Seed lookalikes from video engagement, not only website visits
Build TikTok retargeting from site visitors and product viewers, excluding recent buyers
Build a TikTok retargeting audience directly from Shop activity
Give product specific TikTok search keywords their own ad group

name: Set up TikTok Shop, Search and GMV Max

Launch GMV Max on the top 20 percent of SKUs with an ROI target above break even

name: Check TikTok video creative meets platform spec

Confirm captions and text overlays sit inside the safe zone

Run a 4 week targeting ladder, one layer added per week

Leave spending power and household income targeting alone unless proven otherwise

Wait for a new audience to finish populating before launching on it

name: Design Google campaign architecture and defaults

encompasses: Give every campaign exactly one funnel job and check for overlaps
Default to one campaign per job; require a written reason for every extra split
Run one campaign per country; never two locations in one PMax

Name every campaign with one consistent pattern
Kill tiny orphan campaigns and roll their spend into the top campaigns
Set Sales objective and Purchase only conversion goal on every new campaign
Turn off Search Partners and Display Network on every Search campaign
Use Presence location targeting by default, not Presence or interest
Turn off tablets and TV screens by default, unless the store's own device data says otherwise
Restructure the account toward fewer, fuller campaigns with a written reason for each

name: Run and optimise Google Shopping campaigns
what: Start a new account on Standard Shopping, launch bestsellers only in one ad group, then pick a structure that matches catalog size and margin spread, and run the weekly loop of structure, bidding, negatives and products.
encompasses: Start a new account on Standard Shopping, not PMax; decline the PMax preselection
Launch the first Shopping campaign on bestsellers only, in one ad group
Pick a Shopping structure that matches catalog size and margin spread
Run the Shopping optimisation loop weekly: structure, bidding, negatives, products
